titre: External power supply or USB-C charger sold in France: what the seller must hold before the sale
perimetre: A mains-powered external power supply or USB-C charger (AC input, DC output) placed or made available on the market in France, resold unchanged under the original brand or sold under the seller's own brand, alone or supplied with another device; the file is written for a product with no radio function and no battery, and when the seller answers that it has one, the lines for Directive 2014/53/EU and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 show the main conformity duties only; Union acts only, read on the reference date; the file lists the documents, markings and information each role must hold or check and never states that a product complies.

criteres.question: Under which brand do you sell the product?

valeurs.libelle: Under my own name or trade mark
Unchanged, under the original brand of the company that made it

criteres.aide: Look at the name printed on the product and its packaging: is it yours or the original maker's?

criteres.question: Where is your company established?

valeurs.libelle: In France
In another Member State of the European Union
Outside the European Union

criteres.aide: The country of the registered office of the company that sells.

criteres.question: Where do you get the product from?

valeurs.libelle: From outside the EU: nobody has placed it on the EU market before me
From a supplier established in another EU Member State, who has already placed it on the EU market
From a supplier established in France, who has already placed it on the EU market

criteres.aide: Look at the supplier invoice: the country of the company that sold you the goods.

criteres.question: Has the manufacturer appointed, by written mandate, an authorised representative established in the EU?
criteres.aide: Ask your supplier; an authorised representative is usually named on the declaration of conformity or on the packaging.

criteres.question: Is the charger sold alone or supplied with another device?

valeurs.libelle: Sold alone

Supplied with a radio device of one of these kinds: handheld mobile phone, tablet, digital camera, headphones, headset, handheld videogame console, portable speaker, e-reader, keyboard, mouse, portable navigation system, earbuds, laptop
Supplied with another kind of device

criteres.aide: A device has a radio function when it uses, for example, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a mobile network. The list is Annex Ia, Part I, point 1 of Directive 2014/53/EU.

criteres.question: Do you offer the product online or by another means of distance selling to buyers in France?
criteres.aide: Your own web shop, a marketplace listing, mail order or phone order.

criteres.question: Is the offer addressed to consumers?
criteres.aide: Yes if private individuals can buy it, no if you sell only to businesses.

criteres.question: When are the units first supplied on the EU market?

valeurs.libelle: From 1 April 2020 to 13 December 2028
On or after 14 December 2028

criteres.aide: The date of the first supply of each unit on the EU market, not the date of your own resale. Leave unanswered for a unit first supplied before 1 April 2020: the act that applied then, Regulation (EC) No 278/2009, is not in the source texts.

criteres.question: What input voltage is the product rated for?

valeurs.libelle: Alternating current between 50 V and 1 000 V (for example 100-240 V AC mains)
Direct current between 75 V and 1 500 V
Below 50 V AC and below 75 V DC
Above 1 000 V AC or above 1 500 V DC

criteres.aide: Read the INPUT line of the rating label, for example "100-240V~ 50/60Hz".

criteres.question: Does the product intentionally emit or receive radio waves for the purpose of radio communication or radiodetermination (for example Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or NFC)?
criteres.aide: Look at the datasheet: a plain wired mains charger has no radio function. Whether wireless power transfer alone counts is not settled by the source texts, which speak only of radio communication and radiodetermination.

criteres.question: Does the product contain a battery, or is it a battery (for example a power bank)?
criteres.aide: A battery is a device delivering electrical energy generated by direct conversion of chemical energy (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Article 3(1), point (1)). A plain mains charger contains none.

criteres.question: Is the product one of these: electrical equipment for use in an explosive atmosphere; electrical equipment for radiology and medical purposes; electrical parts for goods and passenger lifts; electricity meter; plug or socket outlet for domestic use; electric fence controller; specialised electrical equipment for use on ships, aircraft or railways which complies with the safety provisions drawn up by international bodies in which the Member States participate; custom built evaluation kit destined for professionals to be used solely at research and development facilities for such purposes?
criteres.aide: The list is Annex II to Directive 2014/35/EU; its item "Radio-electrical interference" is a phenomenon, not a product, and is left out of the question. Reading of this file, not stated by the text: a charger that plugs into a socket is treated as a power supply, not as a "plug or socket outlet for domestic use".

criteres.question: Does the product convert the mains AC input into one or more lower voltage DC or AC outputs?
criteres.aide: Compare the INPUT and OUTPUT lines of the rating label (for example input 100-240 V AC, output 5 V to 20 V DC).

criteres.question: Is the power supply in a physical enclosure separate from the device it powers, connected to it by a cable or connector?
criteres.aide: Yes for a wall charger or a power brick; no for a power supply built inside the device.

criteres.question: What is the nameplate output power?

valeurs.libelle: 250 W or less
More than 250 W

criteres.aide: Read the output power in watts on the rating label or the datasheet, for example "20V 3.25A" or "65W".

criteres.question: Is the product one of these: voltage converter, uninterruptible power supply, battery charger without power supply function, lighting converter, active power over Ethernet injector, docking station for an autonomous appliance?
criteres.aide: The list is Article 1(2), points (a) to (d), (f) and (g) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782; a mains charger that powers a phone or a laptop through a cable is none of them.

criteres.question: What kind of equipment is the charger meant to power?

valeurs.libelle: Household appliances: appliances for cooking and other processing of food, preparing beverages, opening or sealing containers or packages, cleaning, and maintenance of clothes; appliances for hair cutting, hair drying, hair treatment, tooth brushing, shaving, massage and other body care; electric knives; scales; clocks, watches and equipment for measuring, indicating or registering time
Information technology equipment intended primarily for use in the domestic environment (including copying and printing equipment and set-top boxes)

Consumer equipment: radio sets, video cameras, video recorders, hi-fi recorders, audio amplifiers, home theatre systems, televisions, musical instruments, other equipment for recording or reproducing sound or images

Electrical and electronic toys, leisure and sports equipment: electric trains or car racing sets, game consoles including hand-held game consoles, sports equipment with electric or electronic components, other toys, leisure and sports equipment
A medical device
None of the above

criteres.aide: The first four kinds are the four points of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1782. The Annex does not name mobile phones or tablets and this file does not decide under which point they fall: leave the question unanswered if you are unsure.

criteres.question: Is the manufacturer named on the product established in the EU?
criteres.aide: Read the manufacturer address printed on the product, its packaging or the accompanying document. The country of manufacture ("Made in ...") is not the answer.

roles.pourquoi: You sell the product under your own name or trade mark: the manufacturer is the person who has equipment designed or manufactured and markets it under his name or trade mark, and an importer or distributor who places equipment on the market under his name or trade mark is considered a manufacturer and takes on the manufacturer obligations. This is the rule of Directives 2014/35/EU, 2014/30/EU and 2011/65/EU and of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Directive 2009/125/EC (ecodesign) defines the manufacturer differently: see the ecodesign line.

You are established in the Union, you keep the original brand and you are the first to supply on the Union market a product that comes from a third country: that is what the definition of importer describes.

You sell under the original brand and you are not the importer as defined: either another company has already placed the product on the Union market, or you are established outside the Union, and an importer is a person established within the Union. A person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or the importer, who makes the equipment available on the market is a distributor, and the definition sets no condition of establishment. For a seller outside the Union who ships directly to buyers in France, this is a reading of the definition by elimination that a lawyer should confirm; an online offer targeted at end users in the Union is deemed to be made available on the market.

exigences.titre: An economic operator established in the Union answers for the product

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)

exigences.pourquoi: Article 4 covers products subject to the acts it lists, among them Directives 2009/125/EC, 2011/65/EU, 2014/30/EU and 2014/35/EU; the product is electrical equipment rated for a voltage that brings it under Directive 2011/65/EU. Such a product may be placed on the market only if an economic operator established in the Union is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3). An online offer directed at a Member State counts as making available on the market. The Article applies from 16 July 2021.

obligations.resume: The product may be placed on the market only if there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3): a manufacturer established in the Union, an importer where the manufacturer is not, an authorised representative with a written mandate, or failing those a fulfilment service provider established in the Union.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person. You, as the one placing the product on the market, establish which of these four operators exists for the product before the first sale.

preuves.libelle: Identity of the economic operator established in the Union that answers for this product: a manufacturer established in the Union, an importer, an authorised representative holding a written mandate, or a fulfilment service provider established in the Union

obligations.resume: The name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the contact details, including the postal address, of that economic operator are indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person. You, as the one placing the product on the market, make sure these details appear on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.

preuves.libelle: Name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and contact details, including the postal address, of that economic operator, on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document

exigences.titre: Own-brand seller outside the Union: an operator in the Union has to be designated

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)

exigences.pourquoi: You sell under your own brand from outside the Union, so you are not a manufacturer established in the Union: the product may be placed on the market only if an importer, an authorised representative holding your written mandate or, failing those, a fulfilment service provider established in the Union is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3).

obligations.resume: Where the manufacturer is not established in the Union, the economic operator is an importer, an authorised representative with a written mandate from the manufacturer designating it to perform the tasks of Article 4(3) on the manufacturer's behalf, or a fulfilment service provider established in the Union for the products it handles where none of the others is established in the Union.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person. You, as manufacturer outside the Union, arrange for one of these operators; where it is an authorised representative, you give it the written mandate.

preuves.libelle: Written mandate from the manufacturer designating the authorised representative for the tasks of Article 4(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (only where the operator in the Union is an authorised representative)

exigences.titre: Seller outside the Union under the original brand: an operator in the Union must exist before you sell

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)

exigences.pourquoi: You are established outside the Union and you bring in yourself a product sold under its original brand, so no importer as defined stands between you and the buyer (an importer is established within the Union). The product may be placed on the market only if an economic operator established in the Union is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3): a manufacturer established in the Union, an authorised representative holding the written mandate of the manufacturer or, failing those, a fulfilment service provider established in the Union for the products it handles. An online offer targeted at end users in the Union counts as making available on the market.

obligations.resume: The product may be placed on the market only if there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3) in respect of that product.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person. You are the one who first supplies the product on the Union market: before selling, establish which operator established in the Union answers for it.

preuves.libelle: Identity of the economic operator established in the Union that answers for this product: a manufacturer established in the Union, an importer, an authorised representative holding a written mandate, or a fulfilment service provider established in the Union

obligations.resume: The name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the contact details, including the postal address, of that economic operator are indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person. You ship the parcel: make sure these details appear on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.

preuves.libelle: Name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and contact details, including the postal address, of that economic operator, on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document

exigences.titre: Electrical safety: technical file, EU declaration of conformity, CE marking and identification

acte.nom: Directive 2014/35/EU (Low Voltage Directive)

exigences.pourquoi: The Directive applies to electrical equipment designed for use with a voltage rating of between 50 and 1 000 V AC or between 75 and 1 500 V DC, other than the equipment listed in Annex II. The product is rated for an input in that range, is none of the Annex II items and has no radio function, so the rule that takes radio equipment out of this Directive does not come into play.

obligations.resume: When placing their electrical equipment on the market, manufacturers ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the safety objectives referred to in Article 3 and set out in Annex I.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, make sure the design and the manufacture meet the safety objectives; the technical documentation is where this is shown. Annex I, which sets out the objectives, is not in the source texts of this file.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation, electrical safety part (Directive 2014/35/EU, Annex III, Module A, point 2: risk analysis, drawings and schemes, standards applied, test reports)

obligations.resume: The manufacturer establishes technical documentation that makes it possible to assess conformity and includes an analysis and assessment of the risks, containing, where applicable, at least a general description, drawings and schemes, the list of standards applied or the solutions adopted, design calculations and test reports.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, establish the technical documentation. Under Article 10 this also holds when another company makes the product and you place it on the market under your own name or trade mark.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation, electrical safety part (Directive 2014/35/EU, Annex III, Module A, point 2: risk analysis, drawings and schemes, standards applied, test reports)

obligations.resume: Manufacturers draw up the technical documentation and carry out the conformity assessment procedure of Annex III or have it carried out; where compliance with the safety objectives has been demonstrated by that procedure, they draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, carry out the assessment or have it carried out, then draw up the EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation, electrical safety part (Directive 2014/35/EU, Annex III, Module A, point 2: risk analysis, drawings and schemes, standards applied, test reports)
EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires

CE marking affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly to the product or to its data plate (Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 17(1): where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the equipment, on the packaging and the accompanying documents)

obligations.resume: Where the equipment is subject to more than one Union act requiring an EU declaration of conformity, a single EU declaration is drawn up for all of them, identifying the Union acts concerned with their publication references.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer (the declaration is the manufacturer's document under Article 15(4)), draw up one declaration that names every Union act concerned.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires

obligations.resume: The EU declaration of conformity has the model structure of Annex IV, contains the elements of Module A, is continuously updated and is translated into the language or languages required by the Member State in which the equipment is placed or made available on the market.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, keep the declaration up to date and have it translated as France requires. The language France requires is not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires

obligations.resume: Manufacturers ensure that the equipment they have placed on the market bears a type, batch or serial number or other element allowing its identification or, where its size or nature does not allow it, that the information is on the packaging or in an accompanying document.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, have the identification element put on the product.

preuves.libelle: Type, batch or serial number or other identification element on the product (or, where its size or nature does not allow it, on the packaging or an accompanying document)

obligations.resume: Manufacturers indicate on the equipment their name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the postal address at which they can be contacted, a single contact point, or, where that is not possible, on its packaging or in an accompanying document, in a language easily understood by end-users and market surveillance authorities.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, have your own name and postal address put on the product.

preuves.libelle: Manufacturer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the product (or, where that is not possible, on the packaging or an accompanying document)

obligations.resume: Manufacturers ensure that the equipment is accompanied by instructions and safety information in a language which can be easily understood by consumers and other end-users, as determined by the Member State concerned, and that they are clear, understandable and intelligible.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, supply the instructions and safety information with each unit, in the language determined by France.

preuves.libelle: Instructions and safety information accompanying each unit, in the language determined by France

obligations.resume: Manufacturers keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the equipment has been placed on the market.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, keep both documents for 10 years.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation, electrical safety part (Directive 2014/35/EU, Annex III, Module A, point 2: risk analysis, drawings and schemes, standards applied, test reports)
EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires

obligations.resume: Before placing the equipment on the market, importers ensure that the manufacturer has carried out the appropriate conformity assessment procedure and drawn up the technical documentation, that the equipment bears the CE marking and is accompanied by the required documents, and that the manufacturer has complied with Article 6(5) and (6).
obligations.qui_agit: You, as importer, check these points with the manufacturer and on the product before the first sale in the Union.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation of the manufacturer, obtainable on request for the market surveillance authorities

CE marking affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly to the product or to its data plate (Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 17(1): where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the equipment, on the packaging and the accompanying documents)
Type, batch or serial number or other identification element on the product (or, where its size or nature does not allow it, on the packaging or an accompanying document)
Manufacturer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the product (or, where that is not possible, on the packaging or an accompanying document)

obligations.resume: Importers indicate on the equipment their name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the postal address at which they can be contacted or, where that is not possible, on its packaging or in an accompanying document, in a language easily understood by end-users and market surveillance authorities.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as importer, add your own name and postal address.

preuves.libelle: Importer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the product (or, where that is not possible, on the packaging or an accompanying document)

obligations.resume: Importers ensure that the equipment is accompanied by instructions and safety information in a language which can be easily understood by consumers and other end-users, as determined by the Member State concerned.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as importer, make sure each unit ships with the instructions and safety information in the language determined by France.

preuves.libelle: Instructions and safety information accompanying each unit, in the language determined by France

obligations.resume: For 10 years after the equipment has been placed on the market, importers keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities and ensure that the technical documentation can be made available to those authorities on request.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as importer, obtain a copy of the declaration from the manufacturer, keep it for 10 years and secure access to the technical documentation.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires
Technical documentation of the manufacturer, obtainable on request for the market surveillance authorities

obligations.resume: Before making the equipment available on the market, distributors verify that it bears the CE marking, that it is accompanied by the required documents and by instructions and safety information in a language which can be easily understood by consumers and other end-users in the Member State of sale, and that the manufacturer and the importer have complied with Article 6(5) and (6) and Article 8(3) respectively.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as distributor, verify each of these items on the product and its packaging before selling. The importer details are expected only where the product was imported.

preuves.libelle: CE marking affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly to the product or to its data plate (Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 17(1): where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the equipment, on the packaging and the accompanying documents)
Instructions and safety information accompanying each unit, in the language determined by France
Type, batch or serial number or other identification element on the product (or, where its size or nature does not allow it, on the packaging or an accompanying document)
Manufacturer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the product (or, where that is not possible, on the packaging or an accompanying document)
Importer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the product (or, where that is not possible, on the packaging or an accompanying document)

obligations.resume: Economic operators, on request, identify to the market surveillance authorities any economic operator who has supplied them with the equipment and any economic operator to whom they have supplied it, and are able to present that information for 10 years after they have been supplied and for 10 years after they have supplied.
obligations.qui_agit: You, whatever your role, keep track of who supplied you and of the economic operators you supplied, so that you can name them on request for 10 years.

preuves.libelle: Identity of the economic operators who supplied you with the product and of the economic operators you supplied it to, available on request for 10 years (Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 11; Directive 2014/30/EU, Article 12; Directive 2011/65/EU, Article 12)

exigences.titre: Electromagnetic compatibility: technical file behind the same declaration and CE marking

acte.nom: Directive 2014/30/EU (Electromagnetic Compatibility Directive)

exigences.pourquoi: The Directive applies to equipment, which includes any apparatus: a finished appliance made available as a single functional unit, intended for the end-user and liable to generate electromagnetic disturbance or to be affected by it. A mains charger sold to end-users is a finished appliance of that kind. The Directive does not apply to equipment covered by Directive 1999/5/EC, a reference that is now read as a reference to Directive 2014/53/EU: with no radio function the product is not radio equipment and that exclusion does not come into play. Equipment must meet the essential requirements of Annex I.

obligations.resume: Manufacturers draw up the technical documentation of Annex II or Annex III and carry out the relevant conformity assessment procedure or have it carried out; where compliance has been demonstrated by that procedure, they draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, compile the technical documentation, have the assessment carried out, draw up the EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking. Under Article 11 this also holds when another company makes the product and you place it on the market under your own name or trade mark.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation, electromagnetic compatibility part (Directive 2014/30/EU, Annex II or III)
EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires

CE marking affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly to the product or to its data plate (Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 17(1): where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the equipment, on the packaging and the accompanying documents)

obligations.resume: The EU declaration of conformity has the model structure of Annex IV, contains the elements of the relevant modules, is continuously updated and is translated into the language or languages required by the Member State in which the apparatus is placed or made available on the market.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, cover this Directive in the declaration, keep it up to date and have it translated as France requires.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires

obligations.resume: Manufacturers ensure that apparatus which they have placed on the market bear a type, batch or serial number or other element allowing their identification or, where the size or nature of the apparatus does not allow it, that the required information is provided on the packaging or in a document accompanying the apparatus.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, have the identification element put on the product.

obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, have your own name and postal address put on the product.

preuves.libelle: Manufacturer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the product (or, where that is not possible, on the packaging or an accompanying document)

obligations.qui_agit: You, as manufacturer, supply these instructions and information with each unit, in the language determined by France.

preuves.libelle: Instructions and the information referred to in Article 18 of Directive 2014/30/EU (precautions for assembly, installation, maintenance and use; any restriction of use in residential areas) accompanying each unit, in the language determined by France

exigences.titre: Radio equipment (the product itself has a radio function): technical file, EU declaration of conformity and CE marking under Directive 2014/53/EU

acte.nom: Directive 2014/53/EU (Radio Equipment Directive)

exigences.pourquoi: You answered that the product intentionally emits or receives radio waves for radio communication or radiodetermination: it is radio equipment. Radio equipment is not subject to Directive 2014/35/EU, and Directive 2014/30/EU does not apply to equipment covered by Directive 1999/5/EC, a reference now read as a reference to Directive 2014/53/EU. Safety and electromagnetic compatibility do not disappear: they are essential requirements of Directive 2014/53/EU, with no voltage limit applying. exigences.titre: Ecodesign of the external power supply: efficiency file, EC declaration, nameplate and manual information

acte.nom: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1782 (ecodesign requirements for external power supplies)

exigences.pourquoi: The product meets the facts of the definition of an external power supply: it converts mains AC input into a lower voltage output, sits in an enclosure separate from the device it powers, has a nameplate output power not exceeding 250 W and is used with household or office equipment of one of the four kinds listed in Annex I; it is none of the device types the Regulation excludes. The Regulation applies from 1 April 2020 (the act it replaced from that date, Regulation (EC) No 278/2009, is not in the source texts) and is repealed with effect from 14 December 2028, except as provided in Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2025/2052: spare part external power supplies until 14 December 2033 and point 1 of Annex II for supplies with a USB-PD port above 100 W until 14 December 2030. Products covered by such an implementing measure may be placed on the market only if they comply with it and bear the CE marking, under articles of Directive 2009/125/EC that remain in force for them. A unit placed on the market between 14 December 2025 and 14 December 2028 that meets Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 is considered to comply with Regulation (EU) 2019/1782. Who is the manufacturer here: Directive 2009/125/EC has no own-brand rule like the other acts. Its manufacturer is the person who manufactures the product and is responsible for its conformity under its own name or trade mark; a person established in the Community who places a product from a third country on the market is the importer; only in the absence of such a manufacturer or importer is whoever places the product on the market considered the manufacturer. The duties below are shown to an own-brand seller, but this file does not ask who actually manufactures the product and does not decide which of these three cases applies.

obligations.qui_agit: You, where you are the manufacturer within the meaning of Directive 2009/125/EC (see why this line applies), compile the file with the measurement results.

exigences.pourquoi: You offer the product online or by another means of distance selling to consumers, so it is deemed to be made available on the market. The Regulation applies from 13 December 2024.

exigences.titre: General safety requirement for the risks no harmonisation act covers (product outside the Low Voltage Directive)

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (General Product Safety Regulation)

exigences.pourquoi: The product is offered to consumers, so it is a product within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2023/988. Its input voltage puts it outside Directive 2014/35/EU and it has no radio function, so neither that Directive nor Directive 2014/53/EU regulates its safety. Where a product is subject to Union harmonisation legislation, Chapter II of the Regulation is set aside only insofar as the risks covered by that legislation are concerned. This file reads Directives 2014/30/EU and 2011/65/EU as not covering electrical safety, which leaves the general safety requirement of Article 5 for that risk: a reading a lawyer should confirm. Chapter III, Section 1 (the detailed duties of manufacturers, importers and distributors) does not apply to a product subject to harmonisation legislation, so the line carries the requirement itself and no document named by the Regulation. The Regulation applies from 13 December 2024.

obligations.resume: Economic operators place or make available on the market only safe products.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as an economic operator, sell the product only if it is safe as defined in Article 3, point (2). Article 5 names no document; the articles on how safety is assessed are not in the source texts of this file.

preuves.libelle: What you rely on to regard the product as safe for the risks that Directives 2014/30/EU and 2011/65/EU do not cover (Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2023/988 names no document)

exigences.titre: Charger supplied with a phone, tablet, laptop or similar radio device: offer without charger and pictogram

acte.nom: Directive 2014/53/EU (Radio Equipment Directive), as amended by Directive (EU) 2022/2380

exigences.pourquoi: The charger itself is not radio equipment, but it is supplied with radio equipment of a category listed in Annex Ia, Part I. The duties below attach to the offer of that radio equipment together with a charging device. Member States apply these rules from 28 December 2024 for points 1.1 to 1.12 of the list and from 28 April 2026 for laptops.

obligations.resume: Where an economic operator offers consumers and other end-users the possibility to acquire the radio equipment together with a charging device, it also offers them the possibility of acquiring that radio equipment without any charging device.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the economic operator making the offer, also offer the device without the charger.

preuves.libelle: Offer of the same radio equipment without any charging device

obligations.resume: Economic operators ensure that the information on whether or not a charging device is included is displayed with the pictogram of Annex Ia, Part III, printed on the packaging or affixed to it as a sticker, displayed visibly and legibly and, in distance selling, close to the price indication.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the economic operator making the device available, make sure the pictogram is on the packaging and, for distance selling, next to the price.

preuves.libelle: Pictogram showing whether a charging device is included (Directive 2014/53/EU, Annex Ia, Part III), on the packaging and, in distance selling, close to the price

exigences.titre: Waste equipment (WEEE): producer because you sell in France under your own brand

acte.nom: Directive 2012/19/EU (waste electrical and electronic equipment, WEEE)

exigences.pourquoi: The product is electrical and electronic equipment, and from 15 August 2018 the Directive covers all such equipment. You are established in France and market or resell the equipment there under your own name or trade mark, which is the first or second case of the definition of producer. The financing duty concerns waste from private households, a notion that takes in waste from equipment likely to be used by both private households and other users, whoever buys it.

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that each producer, or its authorised representative where one is appointed, is registered as required and can enter online in the national register the information reflecting its activities in that Member State.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the producer for France, register in the French register of producers. The Directive is addressed to Member States: the French procedure is not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: Registration as producer in the national register for France (Article 16(2)(a) of Directive 2012/19/EU names no document; the French procedure is not sourced)

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that producers mark the equipment placed on the market with the crossed-out wheeled bin symbol of Annex IX; only in exceptional cases, because of the size or the function of the product, is the symbol printed on the packaging, the instructions for use and the warranty.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the producer for France, have the symbol printed on the product. The binding wording for France is in French law, which is not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: Crossed-out wheeled bin symbol on the product (Directive 2012/19/EU, Annex IX)

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that producers provide at least for the financing of the collection, treatment, recovery and environmentally sound disposal of waste equipment from private households deposited at collection facilities.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the producer for France, provide for that financing. How this is organised in France is not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: How the financing of the collection, treatment, recovery and disposal of household waste equipment is provided for (Article 12(1) names no document; the French arrangement is not sourced)

exigences.titre: Waste equipment (WEEE): producer because you sell at a distance into France from another country

acte.nom: Directive 2012/19/EU (waste electrical and electronic equipment, WEEE)

exigences.pourquoi: The product is electrical and electronic equipment. You sell it by means of distance communication directly to users in France while established in another Member State or in a third country, which is the fourth case of the definition of producer, whatever the brand. The register of producers also covers producers supplying by distance communication. The financing duty concerns waste from private households, a notion that takes in waste from equipment likely to be used by both private households and other users, whoever buys it.

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that each producer, or its authorised representative where one is appointed, is registered as required and can enter online in the national register the information reflecting its activities in that Member State.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the producer for France, or the authorised representative you appoint, are registered in the French register of producers. If you are established in another Member State, see the line on the authorised representative. If you are established in a third country, the Directive text obtained does not say whether you register yourself or through a representative. The Directive is addressed to Member States: the French procedure is not in the source texts.

exigences.titre: Waste equipment (WEEE): a distance seller established in another Member State appoints an authorised representative in France

acte.nom: Directive 2012/19/EU (waste electrical and electronic equipment, WEEE)

exigences.pourquoi: You are established in another Member State and sell by means of distance communication directly to users in France, which makes you a producer under the fourth case of the definition. A producer of that kind that sells to a Member State in which it is not established appoints an authorised representative there, by written mandate. The duty is laid on the Member State where you are established: its transposition is not in the source texts. The provision is worded for producers established in a Member State and says nothing of a seller in a third country.

obligations.resume: Each Member State shall ensure that a producer selling by distance communication that is established on its territory and sells equipment to another Member State in which it is not established appoints an authorised representative in that Member State as the person responsible for fulfilling its obligations there; the appointment is by written mandate.
obligations.qui_agit: You, as the producer for France, appoint an authorised representative in France by written mandate. The Directive is addressed to Member States: the national rules are not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: Written mandate appointing your authorised representative in France for waste equipment obligations (Directive 2012/19/EU, Article 17(2) and (3))

exigences.titre: Own-brand seller in the Union: you are the operator the authorities turn to

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)

exigences.pourquoi: You sell under your own brand and you are established in the Union: a manufacturer established in the Union is the economic operator responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3).

obligations.resume: The economic operator verifies that the EU declaration of conformity and the technical documentation have been drawn up, keeps the declaration at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities for the period required, ensures that the technical documentation can be made available to them on request, provides information on a reasoned request, informs them when it has reason to believe the product presents a risk, and cooperates with them, including on corrective action.
obligations.qui_agit: You are the Union economic operator for this product: you hold the declaration, can produce the technical documentation on request and answer the market surveillance authorities.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires
Technical documentation of the manufacturer, obtainable on request for the market surveillance authorities

exigences.titre: Importer of a product whose manufacturer is outside the Union: you are the operator the authorities turn to

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance and compliance of products)

exigences.pourquoi: You bring the product into the Union and its manufacturer is not established there: the importer is then an economic operator responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3).

obligations.resume: The economic operator verifies that the EU declaration of conformity and the technical documentation have been drawn up, keeps the declaration at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities for the period required, ensures that the technical documentation can be made available to them on request, provides information on a reasoned request, informs them when it has reason to believe the product presents a risk, and cooperates with them, including on corrective action.
obligations.qui_agit: You are a Union economic operator for this product: you hold a copy of the declaration, can obtain the technical documentation on request and answer the market surveillance authorities.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity: one declaration naming every Union act that requires one, translated as France requires
Technical documentation of the manufacturer, obtainable on request for the market surveillance authorities
